name: Cable Tricep Pushdown V-Bar
description: The V-bar (or triangle bar) pushdown attachment on a high cable creates a pronated grip angle that emphasizes the lateral and medial heads of the tricep. The rigid V-bar allows the lifter to generate maximum downward force with both hands simultaneously without any cable or rope instability. Many lifters find the V-bar pushdown allows the most weight of any pushdown variation, making it effective for strength and hypertrophy.

execution.starting_position: Attach a V-bar to a high cable pulley. Stand facing the cable, grip the V-bar with a pronated grip, elbows at the sides, bar at chest level.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the high cable pulley. The V-bar hangs in a pronated (overhand) position when gripped.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the elbows at the sides and the V-bar at chest/upper abdomen level.
Step 2: Push the V-bar straight down by extending the elbows.
Step 3: Push until the elbows are fully extended.
Step 4: Return with control to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pushdown, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows away from the body
Leaning over the bar to use body weight
Not fully extending the elbows at the bottom
safety_considerations: Keep the elbows pinned to the sides throughout
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Upper arm vertical, full elbow extension at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the triceps at the bottom
